newsitem.title: MEXICO: Frontrunner for Mexico City mayor gets new backing.
newsitem.headline: Frontrunner for Mexico City mayor gets new backing.

text.p: The frontrunner in the race to win election as mayor of Mexico City got an extra boost Wednesday when a left-wing fringe candidate threw in the towel and joined his campaign.
Most polls already put veteran left-winger Cuauhtemoc Cardenas of the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) at least 10 percentage points clear of his nearest opponent for the July 6 election.
Further strengthening his campaign, Cardenas welcomed Francisco Gonzalez, candidate until Tuesday for the minority Workers Party (PT), into his fold.
"Our entry is with enthusiasm, with determination, with fraternity...to combat the evil of neo-liberalism and to defeat the remnants of Salinism," Gonzalez said.
The Mexican left blames Carlos Salinas de Gortari's free market policies during his 1988-94 government for worsening poverty and inequality.
PRD officials at the news conference also threatened to prosecute the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) for what they termed libellous attacks on their party.
The PRI has been losing votes rapidly in recent elections but has tried to fight back by portraying the PRD as a party of violence and confrontation.
Commenting on the attacks, PRD national leader Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador said, "Political desperation tends to lead to the most pathetic inventions".
